title: Statistical Inference for the Factor Model Approach to Estimate Causal Effects in Quasi-Experimental Settings
authors: Kathleen T. Li; Garrett P. Sonnier
eligible_reason: Methods paper on inference for the factor-model (generalized synthetic control) ATT estimator. Both empirical applications have a single treated unit and a single adoption date: (a) California's legalization of recreational marijuana retail sales on January 1, 2018 (beer sales, 41 control states, T1=100, T2=30 weeks); (b) an eyewear e-tailer's Brooklyn showroom opening on July 7, 2011 (52 control cities, T1=76, T2=34 weeks). DiD appears only as a poorly fitting single-cohort benchmark (Figures 7 and 10), alongside synthetic control, modified SC, HCW and factor-model estimates. No staggered adoption, no unit-and-time TWFE specification with multiple cohorts.
design_notes: Factor model y0_it = z_it'beta + lambda_i'F_t + e_it estimated on control units, loadings for the treated unit from pretreatment data, ATT = mean posttreatment gap. Inference theory (Theorems 3.1-3.5) including a multiple-treated-unit extension with unit-specific adoption dates T1i, but the applications are single-unit. Goodman-Bacon, Sun-Abraham, Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess and de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille are cited in a literature paragraph only.
estimators_reported: factor model (Bai 2009 / Xu 2017 generalized synthetic control)

ineligible_specs.exclusion_reason: single treated unit, single adoption date, factor model
single treated unit, single adoption date, factor model

data_availability_statement: No formal statement. Beer data are Nielsen retail scanner data via the Kilts Center (licensed); showroom data are a digitally native eyewear retailer's proprietary city-week sales. Web Appendix H provides MATLAB code and 'a publicly available data set' for the method.
screener_notes: Software is MATLAB (Web Appendix H). Flagged by full-text hits for Borusyak, de Chaisemartin, Goodman-Bacon, Sun-Abraham and 'staggered' because of the literature discussion of heterogeneous-effects DiD; none of those estimators is applied. Not a candidate for re-estimation.
